High-quality studies by Parr and in PLOS ONE found no difference in ratings when wines were tasted on fruit versus root days, and one winemaker’s anecdotal claim aside, the empirical literature is consistent that lunar cycles do not change perceived taste [d4,d5,d7]. In contrast, biodynamic advocates argue that lunar rhythms subtly alter sensory perception, and some retailers schedule tastings according to lunar calendars, but these claims are not supported by controlled evidence [d2,d3,d6]. A single low-credibility blog post claims wines taste the same on fruit and root days, aligning with the empirical findings [d1].

Given this split between rigorous studies and traditional beliefs, the answer is mixed: the best available evidence indicates no lunar effect, yet conflicting opinions persist in practice and popular discourse.
